# MCP Server Instructions

The following MCP servers have provided instructions for how to use their tools and resources:

## blender
You have access to Blender tools to interact with a Blender scene directly.
Blender must be running with the MCP add-on enabled and connected.

IMPORTANT: Respect existing structure and naming conventions.
NEVER assume missing values - inspect the scene first.
Do not destructively modify objects without confirmation.

# Bundled Manuals

Reference documentation is bundled alongside this server as plain-text RST files.
Search and read them directly with standard text tools (grep, file read, etc.):
  * `data/api/` - Blender Python API reference (RST files per module/class).
    Consult when writing or debugging `bpy` code: operator signatures, type
    properties, enum values, etc.
  * `data/manual/` - Blender user manual (RST files mirroring the official manual structure).
    Consult for conceptual explanations, workflow guidance, and feature overviews.

# Executing Code

The `execute_blender_code` tool runs Python code via `bpy` in the connected Blender instance.

The `execute_blender_code` tool is a last resort, if there are other tools that provide
the functionality you need, use those instead.

Prefer operators (`bpy.ops`) for standard actions (adding primitives, applying modifiers,
setting origins) - they handle defaults and context. Use the data API (`bpy.data`) for
precise control or to avoid side effects.

Many operators depend on the current mode (Object, Edit, Sculpt, etc.) and which objects
are active/selected. Verify or set the mode first - wrong mode either fails or silently
does nothing.

The **active object** and **selection** are distinct. Many operators require both.
Set them explicitly - do not assume the current state. Operators change selection and
active state as a side effect, so re-set both between sequential operator calls on
different objects.

Update the dependency graph after changes before reading computed properties
(world matrices, modifier results, etc.).

In edit mode, access mesh geometry through the bmesh API, not the regular mesh data API.
Flush bmesh changes back to the mesh - forgetting this silently loses all edits.

Return structured data (dicts, lists) from executed code, not print output.

# Scene & Data Structure

Blender uses a datablock system - objects and their underlying data (meshes, materials,
cameras, etc.) are separate entities.

Hierarchy:
  * **Scene** - top-level container. A .blend can have multiple.
  * **View Layer** - controls collection visibility/selectability.
  * **Collection** - organizational tree. Objects live in collections; can be nested;
    objects can belong to multiple collections.
  * **Object** - has a transform (location, rotation, scale) and references underlying data
    (Mesh, Curve, Camera, etc.). Multiple objects can share the same data (linked duplicates).
  * **Datablocks** - the actual data: geometry, materials, textures, etc.

Key concepts:
  * Objects and data are separate - deleting one does not delete the other.
  * Orphaned datablocks (zero users) are purged on save/reload or manual purge.
  * Objects created via the data API must be linked to a collection to appear in a scene.
  * Shared data: check user count before modifying a datablock - editing a shared mesh
    affects all objects referencing it. Make single-user first if needed.
  * In most cases file assets:
    * Images, Fonts, Sounds, other `.blend` files -  corraspond to a data-block.

Visibility has three independent states:
  * **Viewport hidden** - still fully scriptable.
  * **Disabled in view layer** - excluded; may be inaccessible to view-layer-dependent operators.
  * **Disabled for render** - skipped during render, otherwise normal.
Check these when objects seem "missing" or operators skip them.

Blender defaults to meters. Check scene unit settings before creating dimensioned objects.

Exploring scenes:
  * Walk the collection hierarchy for an overview first.
  * Don't dump entire scenes - inspect progressively for large scenes.
  * Check object types, parenting, modifiers, and materials before making changes.

# Object Types & Creation

Object types: Mesh, Curve, Su… [truncated]

## claude.ai Claude Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>\n\n<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>\n\n<?claude block s1?>\n\n<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

# Spec §11 — decisions: Codec export (road map "codec-export", #377)

Part of spec §11, *Decisions made — do not re-litigate*. The index of every decision is
[`README.md`](README.md).

The road map that makes these is `designs/codec-export.md` (in progress); its spike record
(`## S — the spike`) holds every measurement cited here. CX-1..CX-11 were recorded in C0,
before any code. Each is marked "owner" (the owner's choice, 2026-10-27) or "default" (the
orchestrator's default, which the owner can still change by a new entry here).

- **CX-1 — The road map: bundled software encoders, four export rows** (owner, 2026-10-27:
  "It is super valuable to me. Bundle the encoders."). Frame Job exports AV1 and VP9 with
  encoders built into the app, as four rows:
  1. AV1 in MP4, with AAC audio;
  2. AV1 in WebM, with Opus audio;
  3. VP9 in WebM, with Opus audio;
  4. VP9 with alpha in WebM.

  VP9 in MP4 is not wanted: it works (the spike measured it) but carries no alpha and is less
  efficient than AV1 in MP4, so it does nothing another row does not. AV1 with alpha is not
  wanted because none exists in practice: neither SVT-AV1's nor libaom's API takes an alpha
  input, and the Matroska AV1 mapping defines none. **Risk accepted:** software encoding is
  1.5–5.4× slower than VideoToolbox's HEVC per 1080p frame on the spike's M2 Max and needs
  1.0–2.1 GB, and the app grows by about 5 MB.

- **CX-2 — AV1 is SVT-AV1 v4.2.0 alone; there is no libaom** (owner). Its three speeds are
  Faster = preset 8, Balanced = preset 6 (the default) and Smaller file = preset 4. The
  spike measured SVT-AV1 at about 3× libaom's speed at matched quality (SVT 4 ≈ libaom
  good-5/6), and better quality at every matched speed; libaom's best tier (good-3/4) was
  about 0.8 VMAF above SVT 4 at about 11× the time. Presets 10 and 12 were within 0–0.7 VMAF
  of HEVC at 2–3× its CPU cost, so they get no row. **Risk accepted:** SVT-AV1's worst frame
  (VMAF 86–88) is lower than libaom's (92), and its memory is higher (1.0–2.1 GB against
  0.5–1.1 GB).

- **CX-3 — VP9 is libvpx v1.17.0 at `--good` cpu-used 4 with row-mt, one speed** (owner).
  VP9's reason to be on the sheet is web playback and alpha, not efficiency: at matched
  quality it needs 1.4–1.7× SVT 6's bitrate. cpu-used 2 bought +0.14–0.43 VMAF for about 35 %
  more time, and rt-8 only matched HEVC, so neither gets a row. **Risk accepted:** one speed,
  so no faster VP9 for a long export.

- **CX-4 — The encoders are platform-side** (default). Swift calls their C APIs through the
  bridging header (`app/Bridging/FrameJob-Bridging-Header.h`); no `rc_*` export wraps them and
  the core never links them, because encoding is sample work and the core does none (spec
  §7). They are arm64, static (each `.a` linked by its full path into the app's one
  executable, never a dylib) and encoder-only (SVT-AV1 `BUILD_DEC=OFF`, libvpx
  `--disable-vp8 --disable-vp9-decoder`). "No ffmpeg dependency in the product" stands: these
  are two encoder libraries, not ffmpeg. **Risk accepted:** the encoders' C APIs become part
  of the Swift side's surface, and an encoder bug crashes the app rather than a helper.

- **CX-5 — The build policy** (default):
  1. Each library is a pinned release tarball checked by SHA-256, fetched and built by
     `make codecs` and by Xcode's "Build Codecs" pre-build step
     (`tools/codecs/build_codecs.py`), installed into `build/codecs/` and reused while its
     stamp's key (the script's bytes, the pins, the tool versions and the deployment target)
     and every recorded output's digest match.
  2. No library source is in git (about 16.7 MB of tarballs stay out). The tools are cmake
     from Homebrew and the system's perl (`/usr/bin/perl`); no nasm, yasm, meson or ninja.
  3. A downloaded tarball whose digest is not the pin's fails the build, naming both digests,
     and is deleted.
  4. Each library's licence and patent texts ship in the bundle at
     `Contents/Resources/Licenses/<library>/`, copied from the source tree; the
     acknowledgements (#376) list them.

  **Risk accepted:** cmake on every build machine and the publish runner, network for the
  first fetch, and a clean build of about one to two minutes.

- **CX-6 — The WebM writer is Rust in `core/`, beside #216-R's reader, not libwebm** (owner).
  Writing container bytes is not sample work, under #216-R's precedent (`deepening.md`): the
  writer decides timestamps, cluster and cue placement and CodecDelay, and touches compressed
  packets only as opaque bytes. It honours spec §7.8's chapters, range and size and #337's
  audio length, so the WebM rows are not a lesser second writer, and it is round-trip tested
  against the reader in `make test`. **Risk accepted:** a new writer to maintain instead of
  Google's proven muxer, and the reader's grid rule and the writer's timing must agree (the
  spike saw libwebm's millisecond times read back off the grid).

- **CX-7 — Opus comes from AudioToolbox** (default), not libopus. It sits where AAC does:
  after the mix and the loudness gain (`ExportAudioGain`, `ExporterLoudness`). The writer
  builds OpusHead and CodecDelay itself, the pre-skip taken from the converter's `primeInfo`
  (312 frames measured), because Apple's 28-byte cookie is not OpusHead. AV1 in MP4 keeps AAC.
  **Risk accepted:** Apple's VBR came in under the asked rate (72 kb/s for 128 k on a test
  tone), and libopus (+0.32 MB) is the fallback only if a quality or control gap shows up.

- **CX-8 — HDR** (default): the AV1 rows are 10-bit, with HLG or PQ tagged in both the
  bitstream (the sequence header's colour config) and the container (`colr` in MP4, `Colour`
  in WebM), plus HD-5's HDR10 mastering metadata (`mdcv`/`clli`, WebM's MasteringMetadata).
  They take `hevc_10bit`'s place in H-3's rules. VP9 Profile 2 HDR is a later phase of its
  own, WebM only, because VP9's bitstream carries no transfer function and the container must.
  **Risk accepted:** no player's HDR rendering of these files was measured.

- **CX-9 — The rate model keeps the bitrate semantics on every row** (default):
  1. `video_bitrate` is the single-pass VBR target (two passes would compose every frame
     twice);
  2. the Quality tiers apply HEVC's 0.6 factor to AV1 and VP9, and "Format default" is HEVC's
     0.07 bits per pixel per frame;
  3. the efficiency goes to the picture, not the file size, because the owner wants quality
     (2026-10-27): SVT 6 measured +2.8 to +4.8 VMAF over HEVC at HEVC's rate;
  4. **risk accepted:** a rate is a target, and single-pass SVT-AV1 undershot it by 14–22 % on
     5 s clips (libvpx overshot by 5–7 %). C1 re-measures on a full-length export. *Result
     (C1):* on the owner's 55 s 1080p30 clip single-pass VBR at Balanced came in at
     0.667–0.670 of the target in six runs, at "Format default" and at High
     (`designs/codec-export.md`, C1); the owner then chose capped constant quality for the
     AV1 rows, CX-13, which replaces (1) and this item there.

- **CX-10 — On an M1 or M2 the AV1 export still works, but Frame Job cannot preview or
  re-import that file** (default): those Macs have no AV1 decoder, and #216's refusal stands.
  The user guide says so (C1), and playback is a manual check on an M3 or later. **Risk
  accepted:** a user on an M1/M2 exports a file they cannot watch in Frame Job or QuickTime.

- **CX-11 — The working arrangement** (default): the road map is built in the `codecs`
  worktree, each phase gated and merged on its own. C0 adds no export row and no format bump:
  it records these decisions, opens the road map and builds and links the two libraries.

- **CX-12 — C1's shape: AV1 in MP4 at 8 bits** (default, recorded in C1 before its code):
  1. **The row.** `av1`, "AV1 (MP4)", after `hevc_10bit` in the table: MP4, codec `av1`, video
     with AAC audio, no alpha, even-sized as every AVFoundation row but `prores_4444` (G-33).
     Its `avf_preset` is `AVAssetExportPresetPassthrough`, a record only, because
     AVFoundation still writes the container; a new field, `writer` (`svt_av1`), names the
     encoder route, so `avf_preset: null` keeps meaning the ImageIO writer and no other row
     changes.
  2. **The speed.** `encoder_speed` is `faster`, `balanced` (the default) or `smaller` — SVT-AV1
     preset 8, 6 or 4 (CX-2) — and is refused on a row without encoder speeds, naming the key.
     The sheet's Speed row sits under Format (after Dynamic Range when that is shown); on
     another row it is disabled and shows the last choice, as Quality does, and the choice is
     remembered with the rest of the sheet (`ExportChoice`).
  3. **Keyframes.** A closed GOP (`intra_refresh_type` = `SVT_AV1_KF_REFRESH`), a keyframe at
     least every 2 s (`intra_period_length` = ⌊2·fps⌋ − 1). The sync samples are the
     passthrough `AVAssetWriter`'s own, read from the bitstream: C1 measured that marking every
     sample `NotSync` left the file's sync samples at exactly its KEY_FRAMEs, so the pump
     writes no sync attachment, and `av1_export_proof.py` A5's match of each key-flagged
     packet to a shown KEY_FRAME, both ways, is the guard. The `SVT_AV1_KF_REFRESH` line is
     live only under CX-13's capped CRF: SVT-AV1 v4.2.0 forces KF refresh under single-pass
     VBR (`lap_rc`), and under CRF its FWDKF refresh writes each 2 s refresh as a hidden
     INTRA_ONLY frame (`frame_type` 2, `show_frame` 0, shown later by `show_existing_frame`)
     after one KEY_FRAME, which A5 refuses.
  4. **The container bytes are the core's.** The `av1C` record (built from SVT's sequence
     header OBU), the stripping of temporal delimiters from every packet and the rewrite of
     the written file's `ftyp` to carry `av01` are decided in the core (CX-6's container-bytes
     precedent; `rc_av1_*`). A written file whose `ftyp` cannot take `av01` fails the export.
  5. **The frames.** The compositor's 64RGBAHalf frames are converted on the GPU to BT.709
     video-range I420 (chroma the mean of each 2×2 block); when the export size is not the
     canvas, `MPSImageLanczosScale` scales first, fit or fill per G-33 (c), with black bars.
  6. **SVT-AV1's log** goes through `svt_av1_set_log_callback`: info and debug are dropped,
     warnings and errors become `NSLog("SVT-AV1: …")`.
  7. **HDR projects.** In an HLG project the `av1` row writes the SDR version, by HD-14's
     existing rule for an SDR row; 10-bit and HDR AV1 are C2's (CX-8).

- **CX-13 — AV1's rate is a soft cap: capped constant quality, quality first** (owner,
  2026-10-27, "Capped constant quality", chosen after C1 measured single-pass VBR at
  0.667–0.670 of its target on a 55 s 1080p clip; then 2026-10-28, "Quality first, soft
  cap"; amends CX-9 (1) and (4) for the AV1 rows, CX-9 (2) and (3) standing):
  1. **The mode.** SVT-AV1 runs capped CRF: `rate_control_mode` 0 with `aq_mode` 2 (what its
     own `--crf` sets), `qp` the CRF, and `max_bit_rate` the cap — the mode SVT-AV1 v4.2.0's
     `EbSvtAv1Enc.h` documents for `max_bit_rate` and `mbr_over_shoot_pct` ("Capped CRF") and
     its `enc_settings.c` refuses outside rate-control mode 0. `mbr_over_shoot_pct` is SVT's
     own default, 50 (`EbSvtAv1Enc.h` "Default is 50", `enc_settings.c`, `Docs/Parameters.md`),
     so the requested rate is a cap the encoder aims under that hard footage may exceed: at
     (3)'s CRFs on the spike's clips the largest whole-file average was **1.254 × the cap**
     (gh5, 25 fps, Faster at Format default; 14 of 45 files over 1 ×, all of them gh5 but one
     real8 at 1.022 ×), with every file at or above HEVC's VMAF (the least margin +0.035).
     **The tolerance:** `av1_export_proof.py` R1 and R2 hold each file of the owner's clip to
     at most 1.30 × the cap (raised from 1.25 × at integration, above the measured 1.254 ×) and to a VMAF at or above `hevc`'s. **Declined (owner, 2026-10-28):
     a strict cap.** At 12 % overshoot every spike file stayed at or under 0.990 × the cap, but
     the cap then lowers the picture while the file is far under it (SVT holds keyframes and
     base-layer frames to a share of each 60-frame window), and the owner's clip at Faster,
     Format default, plateaued under HEVC's 95.469:

     | Faster, Format default, owner's clip | 12 % overshoot | 50 % overshoot |
     |---|---|---|
     | CRF 24 | 95.055 (0.645 × the cap) | 95.583 (0.729 ×) |
     | CRF 20 | 95.184 (0.703 ×) | 95.919 (0.844 ×) |
     | CRF 16 | 95.348 (0.735 ×) | — |

     (25 % and 20 % held gh5 to 1.03 × and 0.999 × at the first CRFs; at 10 % the cap
     dropped gh5 at Faster's Medium 0.02–0.08 VMAF under HEVC.)

# Spec §11 — decisions: Codec export (road map "codec-export", #377)

Part of spec §11, *Decisions made — do not re-litigate*. The index of every decision is
[`README.md`](README.md).

The road map that makes these is `designs/codec-export.md` (in progress); its spike record
(`## S — the spike`) holds every measurement cited here. CX-1..CX-11 were recorded in C0,
before any code. Each is marked "owner" (the owner's choice, 2026-10-27) or "default" (the
orchestrator's default, which the owner can still change by a new entry here).

- **CX-1 — The road map: bundled software encoders, four export rows** (owner, 2026-10-27:
  "It is super valuable to me. Bundle the encoders."). Frame Job exports AV1 and VP9 with
  encoders built into the app, as four rows:
  1. AV1 in MP4, with AAC audio;
  2. AV1 in WebM, with Opus audio;
  3. VP9 in WebM, with Opus audio;
  4. VP9 with alpha in WebM.

  VP9 in MP4 is not wanted: it works (the spike measured it) but carries no alpha and is less
  efficient than AV1 in MP4, so it does nothing another row does not. AV1 with alpha is not
  wanted because none exists in practice: neither SVT-AV1's nor libaom's API takes an alpha
  input, and the Matroska AV1 mapping defines none. **Risk accepted:** software encoding is
  1.5–5.4× slower than VideoToolbox's HEVC per 1080p frame on the spike's M2 Max and needs
  1.0–2.1 GB, and the app grows by about 5 MB.

- **CX-2 — AV1 is SVT-AV1 v4.2.0 alone; there is no libaom** (owner). Its three speeds are
  Faster = preset 8, Balanced = preset 6 (the default) and Smaller file = preset 4. The
  spike measured SVT-AV1 at about 3× libaom's speed at matched quality (SVT 4 ≈ libaom
  good-5/6), and better quality at every matched speed; libaom's best tier (good-3/4) was
  about 0.8 VMAF above SVT 4 at about 11× the time. Presets 10 and 12 were within 0–0.7 VMAF
  of HEVC at 2–3× its CPU cost, so they get no row. **Risk accepted:** SVT-AV1's worst frame
  (VMAF 86–88) is lower than libaom's (92), and its memory is higher (1.0–2.1 GB against
  0.5–1.1 GB).

- **CX-3 — VP9 is libvpx v1.17.0 at `--good` cpu-used 4 with row-mt, one speed** (owner).
  VP9's reason to be on the sheet is web playback and alpha, not efficiency: at matched
  quality it needs 1.4–1.7× SVT 6's bitrate. cpu-used 2 bought +0.14–0.43 VMAF for about 35 %
  more time, and rt-8 only matched HEVC, so neither gets a row. **Risk accepted:** one speed,
  so no faster VP9 for a long export.

- **CX-4 — The encoders are platform-side** (default). Swift calls their C APIs through the
  bridging header (`app/Bridging/FrameJob-Bridging-Header.h`); no `rc_*` export wraps them and
  the core never links them, because encoding is sample work and the core does none (spec
  §7). They are arm64, static (each `.a` linked by its full path into the app's one
  executable, never a dylib) and encoder-only (SVT-AV1 `BUILD_DEC=OFF`, libvpx
  `--disable-vp8 --disable-vp9-decoder`). "No ffmpeg dependency in the product" stands: these
  are two encoder libraries, not ffmpeg. **Risk accepted:** the encoders' C APIs become part
  of the Swift side's surface, and an encoder bug crashes the app rather than a helper.

- **CX-5 — The build policy** (default):
  1. Each library is a pinned release tarball checked by SHA-256, fetched and built by
     `make codecs` and by Xcode's "Build Codecs" pre-build step
     (`tools/codecs/build_codecs.py`), installed into `build/codecs/` and reused while its
     stamp's key (the script's bytes, the pins, the tool versions and the deployment target)
     and every recorded output's digest match.
  2. No library source is in git (about 16.7 MB of tarballs stay out). The tools are cmake
     from Homebrew and the system's perl (`/usr/bin/perl`); no nasm, yasm, meson or ninja.
  3. A downloaded tarball whose digest is not the pin's fails the build, naming both digests,
     and is deleted.
  4. Each library's licence and patent texts ship in the bundle at
     `Contents/Resources/Licenses/<library>/`, copied from the source tree; the
     acknowledgements (#376) list them.

  **Risk accepted:** cmake on every build machine and the publish runner, network for the
  first fetch, and a clean build of about one to two minutes.

- **CX-6 — The WebM writer is Rust in `core/`, beside #216-R's reader, not libwebm** (owner).
  Writing container bytes is not sample work, under #216-R's precedent (`deepening.md`): the
  writer decides timestamps, cluster and cue placement and CodecDelay, and touches compressed
  packets only as opaque bytes. It honours spec §7.8's chapters, range and size and #337's
  audio length, so the WebM rows are not a lesser second writer, and it is round-trip tested
  against the reader in `make test`. **Risk accepted:** a new writer to maintain instead of
  Google's proven muxer, and the reader's grid rule and the writer's timing must agree (the
  spike saw libwebm's millisecond times read back off the grid).

- **CX-7 — Opus comes from AudioToolbox** (default), not libopus. It sits where AAC does:
  after the mix and the loudness gain (`ExportAudioGain`, `ExporterLoudness`). The writer
  builds OpusHead and CodecDelay itself, the pre-skip taken from the converter's `primeInfo`
  (312 frames measured), because Apple's 28-byte cookie is not OpusHead. AV1 in MP4 keeps AAC.
  **Risk accepted:** Apple's VBR came in under the asked rate (72 kb/s for 128 k on a test
  tone), and libopus (+0.32 MB) is the fallback only if a quality or control gap shows up.

- **CX-8 — HDR** (default): the AV1 rows are 10-bit, with HLG or PQ tagged in both the
  bitstream (the sequence header's colour config) and the container (`colr` in MP4, `Colour`
  in WebM), plus HD-5's HDR10 mastering metadata (`mdcv`/`clli`, WebM's MasteringMetadata).

# Road map "codec-export" — AV1 and VP9 export with bundled encoders (#377)

**Opened 2026-10-27** (C0), in the worktree `~/devel/framejob-codecs` on branch `codecs`, from
`75fd806`; each phase is gated and merged into main alone (CX-11). This road map's decisions are
CX-1 onwards, in `designs/spec/11-decisions/codec-export.md`. Its brief is issue #377; the
acknowledgements its licences feed are #376.

## Goal

Frame Job exports H.264, HEVC (8-bit, 10-bit, with alpha), ProRes and still sequences, all
through AVFoundation and VideoToolbox. After this road map it also exports AV1 and VP9, encoded
by two libraries built into the app (SVT-AV1 and libvpx), into MP4 or WebM, with Opus audio in
WebM and alpha in VP9 WebM.

## The owner's choices

**2026-10-27** (the brief, `request.md`; binding; "It is super valuable to me. Bundle the
encoders."):

- **AV1 encoder: SVT-AV1 only** (pinned v4.2.0). There is no libaom.
  - Three speed choices on the export sheet: Faster = preset 8, Balanced = preset 6 (default),
    Smaller file = preset 4.
- **VP9 encoder: libvpx** (pinned v1.17.0), one speed (cpu-used 4, row-mt).
- **Export rows:** all four of these. VP9-in-MP4 is NOT wanted.
  - AV1 in MP4, with AAC audio;
  - AV1 in WebM, with Opus;
  - VP9 in WebM, with Opus;
  - VP9 + alpha in WebM.
- **WebM writer:** a Rust Matroska/WebM writer in `core/`, next to the import reader, not
  libwebm. Writing container bytes is not sample work, under the precedent of #216-R's reader.

Also the owner's, standing: only higher-quality exports matter (2026-10-27); no feature size
budget; memory limits relative to physical RAM; person-only checks go in
`docs/manual-checks.md`.

## The orchestrator's defaults (each one the owner can change)

- **Opus:** macOS AudioToolbox's Opus encoder, not libopus, after the mix and loudness gain
  (CX-7). *The owner can change this.*
- **HDR:** AV1 at 10 bits with HLG/PQ, plus HDR10 mastering metadata, on the AV1 rows; VP9
  Profile 2 HDR later, WebM only, in its own phase (CX-8). *The owner can change this.*
- **Library sources:** pinned tarballs checked by SHA-256, fetched and built by `make codecs`
  and cached by a stamp; no sources vendored into the repo (CX-5). *The owner can change this.*
- **Rate model:** the bitrate semantics kept on every row, the efficiency spent on the picture
  (CX-9). *The owner can change this.*
- **AV1 decode on M1/M2:** the export works there, but Frame Job cannot preview or re-import
  its own AV1 file; the guide says so (CX-10). *The owner can change this.*
- **The encoders platform-side** (CX-4) and **the working arrangement** (CX-11). *The owner can
  change these.*

## How it fits the tree (at `75fd806`)

- **The export table.** `core/src/export_table.rs` (584) holds each row: `id`, `codec`, the
  container, and `avf_preset` (`None` today means the ImageIO still writer). C1 adds a writer
  field for the encoder rows rather than overloading `avf_preset: None`. `export.rs` (259),
  `export_size.rs` (274) and `export_overrides.rs` (295) are the rest of the settings.
- **The writer.** `app/Sources/ExporterWriter.swift` (586) runs an
  `AVAssetReaderVideoCompositionOutput` of 64RGBAHalf frames into a pump on `videoQueue`;
  `ExporterWriter+Settings.swift` (468) holds `defaultVideoBitrate` (0.07 bits/pixel/frame) and
  the Quality tiers; `+Chapters` (248) the chapters. `Exporter.swift` (598) is at the cap, and
  the encoder path goes in new files. The audio pump reads 48 kHz stereo and gains it once
  (`ExporterAudioGain.swift`, `ExporterLoudness.swift`); `ExportAudioEnd.swift` holds #337's
  length rule.
- **The reader the WebM writer mirrors.** `core/src/container*.rs` (seven files, 2,024 lines
  today): EBML, the headers, the blocks, the timing and its grid rule, Vorbis. The writer goes
  in new modules beside them (CX-6).
- **The build.** `make rust` (cargo, then `project.yml`'s "Build Rust Core" pre-build step) is
  the shape `make codecs` copies (CX-5). `tools/proof/gate.py` stamps each Full step by its
  inputs and tool versions; `tools/proof/swift_build.py` is the one probe build line;
  `tools/proof/tree_copy.py` builds old or mutated trees in copies.
- **The bridge.** `app/Bridging/FrameJob-Bridging-Header.h` imports only the core's header
  today. The encoders' headers join it (CX-4); no `rc_*` export wraps them.

## Phases

- **C0 — decisions and the encoder build; CX-1..CX-11.** CX-1..CX-11 recorded in §11 before
  any code, and this road map with the spike's record. `tools/codecs/build_codecs.py` fetches
  SVT-AV1 v4.2.0 and libvpx v1.17.0 as pinned tarballs, checks each by SHA-256, builds them
  arm64, static and encoder-only at the app's deployment target (26.0), and installs headers,
  archives and licence texts into `build/codecs/`, reused by its stamp. `make codecs`; `app`,
  `app-debug`, `typecheck` and `test` depend on it; `project.yml`'s "Build Codecs" pre-build
  step, the header search path, both archives by full path in every configuration's
  `OTHER_LDFLAGS`, and "Copy Codec Licences" into `Contents/Resources/Licenses/`. One Swift
  file, `CodecLibraries.swift`, reads each library's version and opens an SVT-AV1 handle, behind
  `-RCCodecProbe 1`. The gate, the probe builder, the tree copies, the four spikes' own build
  lines and the publish workflow's cmake. **Acceptance:** `make gate` passes; `dist_check`
  41/41 with a stand-in Sparkle key (D36–D41: the encoder symbols in both executables, no load
  command outside the system and Sparkle, the licences byte-identical in both bundles), its

# Road map "codec-export" — AV1 and VP9 export with bundled encoders (#377)

**Opened 2026-10-27** (C0), in the worktree `~/devel/framejob-codecs` on branch `codecs`, from
`75fd806`; each phase is gated and merged into main alone (CX-11). This road map's decisions are
CX-1 onwards, in `designs/spec/11-decisions/codec-export.md`. Its brief is issue #377; the
acknowledgements its licences feed are #376.

## Goal

Frame Job exports H.264, HEVC (8-bit, 10-bit, with alpha), ProRes and still sequences, all
through AVFoundation and VideoToolbox. After this road map it also exports AV1 and VP9, encoded
by two libraries built into the app (SVT-AV1 and libvpx), into MP4 or WebM, with Opus audio in
WebM and alpha in VP9 WebM.

## The owner's choices

**2026-10-27** (the brief, `request.md`; binding; "It is super valuable to me. Bundle the
encoders."):

- **AV1 encoder: SVT-AV1 only** (pinned v4.2.0). There is no libaom.
  - Three speed choices on the export sheet: Faster = preset 8, Balanced = preset 6 (default),
    Smaller file = preset 4.
- **VP9 encoder: libvpx** (pinned v1.17.0), one speed (cpu-used 4, row-mt).
- **Export rows:** all four of these. VP9-in-MP4 is NOT wanted.
  - AV1 in MP4, with AAC audio;
  - AV1 in WebM, with Opus;
  - VP9 in WebM, with Opus;
  - VP9 + alpha in WebM.
- **WebM writer:** a Rust Matroska/WebM writer in `core/`, next to the import reader, not
  libwebm. Writing container bytes is not sample work, under the precedent of #216-R's reader.

Also the owner's, standing: only higher-quality exports matter (2026-10-27); no feature size
budget; memory limits relative to physical RAM; person-only checks go in
`docs/manual-checks.md`.

## The orchestrator's defaults (each one the owner can change)

- **Opus:** macOS AudioToolbox's Opus encoder, not libopus, after the mix and loudness gain
  (CX-7). *The owner can change this.*
- **HDR:** AV1 at 10 bits with HLG/PQ, plus HDR10 mastering metadata, on the AV1 rows; VP9
  Profile 2 HDR later, WebM only, in its own phase (CX-8). *The owner can change this.*
- **Library sources:** pinned tarballs checked by SHA-256, fetched and built by `make codecs`
  and cached by a stamp; no sources vendored into the repo (CX-5). *The owner can change this.*
- **Rate model:** the bitrate semantics kept on every row, the efficiency spent on the picture
  (CX-9). *The owner can change this.*
- **AV1 decode on M1/M2:** the export works there, but Frame Job cannot preview or re-import
  its own AV1 file; the guide says so (CX-10). *The owner can change this.*
- **The encoders platform-side** (CX-4) and **the working arrangement** (CX-11). *The owner can
  change these.*

## How it fits the tree (at `75fd806`)

- **The export table.** `core/src/export_table.rs` (584) holds each row: `id`, `codec`, the
  container, and `avf_preset` (`None` today means the ImageIO still writer). C1 adds a writer
  field for the encoder rows rather than overloading `avf_preset: None`. `export.rs` (259),
  `export_size.rs` (274) and `export_overrides.rs` (295) are the rest of the settings.
- **The writer.** `app/Sources/ExporterWriter.swift` (586) runs an
  `AVAssetReaderVideoCompositionOutput` of 64RGBAHalf frames into a pump on `videoQueue`;
  `ExporterWriter+Settings.swift` (468) holds `defaultVideoBitrate` (0.07 bits/pixel/frame) and
  the Quality tiers; `+Chapters` (248) the chapters. `Exporter.swift` (598) is at the cap, and
  the encoder path goes in new files. The audio pump reads 48 kHz stereo and gains it once

content.content:
- **HD-5 — The deliverables: HLG, HDR10 (PQ) or SDR on the 10-bit rows, the SDR version on every
  other row; Dolby Vision off; the HDR10 metadata fixed.** Choices 4a, 5a and 6a (owner,
  2026-10-19: "HLG + HDR10, DV off (Recommended)").
  - **The 10-bit rows** (`hevc_10bit`, `prores_422`, `prores_4444`) of an HLG project write HLG
    by default. `export {range: "hlg" | "pq" | "sdr"}` and the export sheet's Dynamic Range
    popup (HLG · HDR10 (PQ) · SDR) choose. `range` is resolved in the core's export resolver,
    per row: the canvas's output for a 10-bit row, `sdr` otherwise. It is a per-export
    argument, not persisted state.
  - **Every other row** (`h264`, `hevc`, `hevc_alpha`, `gif`, `apng`) and JPEG frames write the
    SDR version (HD-4).
  - **Refusals**, each in its own sentence: `hlg` or `pq` on an 8-bit row, and `hlg` or `pq` in
    an SDR project. Until H-3 lands, H-2 refuses every row but the three 10-bit ones in an HLG
    project, so a merged phase never writes HLG pixels labelled BT.709.
  - **Dolby Vision off** (choice 5a): HEVC is written with `kVTHDRMetadataInsertionMode_None`.
    Measured for the brief (M7): without it VideoToolbox adds a Dolby Vision profile 8.4
    configuration and RPU frames to an HLG HEVC Main 10 file by itself; with it, the same
    `bt2020nc/arib-std-b67/bt2020` tags and no Dolby Vision. Every player then shows the HLG
    that was graded.
  - **HDR10's metadata is fixed** (choice 6a): a P3-D65 mastering display at 0.005–1,000
    cd/m², MaxCLL 1,000, MaxFALL 0 ("unknown"), in one pass. True by construction: PQ is HLG
    → display light at 1,000 cd/m² → ST 2084, so nothing exceeds 1,000 cd/m². Measured for the
    brief (M7): explicit values are written exactly, by HEVC and ProRes 422 HQ alike.
  - **Amends GR-19:** PQ becomes an export range, not a `canvas.output` value (GR-19 left PQ "a
    later option" without saying where), and every 8-bit row carries the SDR version, not only
    GIF and APNG ("GIF and APNG stay SDR"). PR-3 stands: `hevc` stays Main and carries the SDR
    version.
  **Amended by HD-14** (hdr H-3): the argument is spelled `dynamic_range`, not `range` (which the
  export tool already takes for `"project"` or `"in_out"`); the settings' `color` and presets'
  `"hdr"` carry it.
- **HD-6 — #281: a PQ media's own peak sets step 0's PQ white; 1,000 cd/m² when unknown.**
  Choice 7a (taken as recommended, stated to the owner before the questions; the owner's
  2026-10-14 comment on #281 asked for it as a feature).
  - **Read at import:** first the format description's mastering-display and content-light
    extensions; failing those, the first video sample's prefix SEI payloads 137 (mastering
    display) and 144 (content light level), parsed by the core from bytes as a pure function
    (Swift reads the bytes). The peak is **MaxCLL when present and non-zero, else the mastering
    display's maximum**.
  - **Stored on the media** (its key and shape H-1's spec names), with `detected` semantics like
    Apple Log's; shown in the Media tab with an override; `set_media_color` takes the override,
    one optional key and no new op; a peak on media that is not PQ is refused by name.
  - **Step 0:** PQ's white is peak/203 instead of 1000/203, held at 1 or above (above the
    knee); an unknown peak means 1,000, so every unlabelled file renders byte-identical.
    Computed for the brief (`hdr_math.py`, levels of 255 at the PQ arm's output): at PQ 0.70
    (620.9 cd/m²) a 600 cd/m² peak gives 255.0, today's 1,000 gives 246.9, 4,000 gives 242.8.
  - **Thumbnails follow** (GR-21), as they follow Camera Log. **Format 22** (HD-11).
----
- **HD-14 — H-3's settlements: the knee at 0.9, one output pass chosen by the key's
  `dynamic_range`, the argument's spelling and its refusals, PQ at 1,000 cd/m² with HD-5's
  metadata, the frames, Show SDR Version's key and the sheet's row.** H-3's spec, recorded before
  its code; it settles what HD-4, HD-5 and HD-7 left to H-3. No format change.
  - **(a) The knee is 0.9**, choice 3a's shape, on the largest linear BT.709 channel over
    reference white (1 = 203 cd/m²), with W = 1000/203 and GR-15's extended-Reinhard shoulder
    after its gamut lift. Recomputed on HD-3's lift by `python3 -I
    tools/proof/work/h3/sdr_version_math.py` (scratch, gitignored; 2026-10-20, AC Power). The lift
    reads 0.10 → 0.13582, 0.42 → 0.43872, 1.00 → 0.74988. At knee 0.9 the levels of 255 are, with
    GR-15's beside them: SDR 0.42 title 107.1 (GR-15 87.4); SDR 0.75 grey 191.2 (127.7); SDR-white
    title **248.4** (154.2); iPhone HLG 0.50 **125.7** (97.1; the brief's 143.1 was BT.1886's);
    HLG 0.85 253.9 (189.4); HLG 0.90 254.4 (209.3); HLG 1.00 255.0. The white title by knee
    0.39/0.5/0.6/0.7/0.75/0.8/0.85/0.9/0.95 reads 212.7/220.7/227.8/234.8/238.3/241.7/245.1/
    248.4/251.7, and 249.6 needs knee 0.9170. The round trip is within 0.5 of a 10-bit level up to
    SDR 0.9531; the knee's SDR grey is 0.9477 (241.7/255). The SDR version at HLG
    0.10/0.25/0.40/0.50/0.60/0.70/0.75/0.80/0.90/1.00 is
    0.06875/0.21101/0.37509/0.49288/0.64091/0.85788/0.97430/0.99102/0.99762/1.00000 (the proof's
    oracle). **BT.2408's own HDR → SDR constants**, read for H-3 (Report ITU-R BT.2408-9, 2026,
    fetched from itu.int on 2026-10-20): the report gives no down-mapping curve or knee of its
    own; §5.2 prefers display-light down-mapping and points to Report BT.2446's three example
    methods, and says a live production's down-mapper follows "a complementary tone-curve to any
    SDR to HDR converters over the lower and middle signal ranges, with compressed highlights
    filling the upper SDR signal range" (a "hybrid-linear" down-mapper) — the shape of this
    choice; §7.1.3 records SDR content at 75 % HLG attenuated on the SDR output "to as little as
    86 % (a 14 % loss)", and round-trip losses "as low as 5 %" where a down-mapper uses the
    super-white range to EBU R.103's ~105 %. Frame Job's SDR deliverable has no super-white, and
    its round trip holds to SDR 0.9531, a loss of about 5 % below SDR white. The knee is unchanged
    by the reading.
  - **(b) One output pass** (`framejob_output_fragment`), for the preview, `render_frame` and
    export, chosen by the recipe key's `dynamic_range` option and drawn only in an HLG project

content.content:
## S — the spike

### Record

**Run 2026-10-27, before C0** (no product code, nothing committed), recorded in
`~/.claude/litecode/framejob/codecs-377/S-spike.md` and copied here: the measurements below,
with each instrument's path in this worktree. `tools/proof/work/` is gitignored, so the
instruments and logs stay in the `~/devel/framejob-codecs` worktree and are not in git. The
spike's phase split became the Phases above, and its eight owner questions were answered on
2026-10-27 ("The owner's choices" above, CX-1..CX-3, CX-6) or taken as the orchestrator's
defaults (CX-4, CX-5, CX-7..CX-10).

Date: 2026-10-27. Host: M2 Max (12 cores: 8 P + 4 E), macOS 26.5.1, AC power, Apple clang 17.0.0.
Worktree: `/Users/kevingalligan/devel/framejob-codecs` (branch `codecs`), no product code
touched, nothing committed. Every instrument, log and output is under
`tools/proof/work/codec-spike/` (gitignored):

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `tools/proof/work/codec-spike/build.sh` | builds one library from pinned source, timed |
| `tools/proof/work/codec-spike/run.py` | one encode: timed with `/usr/bin/time -l`, then VMAF/PSNR/SSIM with ffmpeg's libvmaf |
| `tools/proof/work/codec-spike/batch8.sh`, `tools/proof/work/codec-spike/batch10.sh`, `tools/proof/work/codec-spike/batch-extra.sh` | the sweeps; logs `batch*.log` |
| `tools/proof/work/codec-spike/results.jsonl` (284 runs), `tools/proof/work/codec-spike/analyse.py`, `tools/proof/work/codec-spike/analysis.md` | the raw rows and the tables below |
| `tools/proof/work/codec-spike/probe/size/` | link-size probes (`link.sh`) |
| `tools/proof/work/codec-spike/probe/mux/` | `muxprobe.swift`, `ivfprobe.swift`, `decprobe.swift`, `av1c.py`, `runmux.sh`, `runivf.sh` |
| `tools/proof/work/codec-spike/probe/webm/` | `webmprobe.cc` (libwebm + libopus), `mkalpha.sh`, `runwebm.sh`, `alpha2.sh` |
| `tools/proof/work/codec-spike/probe/opus/opusprobe.swift` | Apple's Opus encoder |
| `tools/proof/work/codec-spike/probe/frames/frameprobe.swift` | frame conversion costs |
| `tools/proof/work/codec-spike/probe/roundtrip/` | a scratch binary over the core's own `container::Container` (#216-R reader) |

**Timing noise.** Another lane (`raster-dither`, a Frame Job Debug at 941 % CPU, then
swift builds) ran throughout: the 1-minute load average read 7–200 across the runs, and
each row records it (`load1_before`). Wall-clock fps from the first sweep is unreliable
(aom good-6 read 3.3–19.4 fps across runs). CPU-seconds per frame is steadier. The speed
table below therefore uses the three runs per config on the real clip at Frame Job's HEVC
rate, two of them repeats taken late, when the load had fallen to 8–50; their spread is
printed. My own rebuilds of the libraries (build-time repeats) overlapped the first sweep,
deleted `aomenc` under three runs (they failed, were re-run in `batch-extra.sh`), and are
part of that sweep's noise. Swift probes here were compiled with plain `swiftc` (they use
no app source; `swift_build.py` is for probes built from `app/Sources`).

### What was measured

#### Test content

150 frames (5 s) of 1080p each, written to y4m so decode cost is out of the timings:

| Clip | Source | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `real8` | `tools/proof/media/owner-sync/IMG_0018.MOV` (iPhone, HEVC Main 10, 1920×1080 30p, HLG), from 10 s | converted to 8-bit `yuv420p` with no tone map (no zscale in this ffmpeg), so the picture is HLG code values seen as SDR — fine as encoder content |
| `real10` | same frames, `yuv420p10le`, HLG | the 10-bit runs |
| `gh5` | GH5 V-Log L "borough market" 4K 25p, scaled to 1080p (lanczos) | busy street scene; 25 fps, so its rate targets are ×25/30 |
| `promo` | `~/Movies/Frame Job Promo.mp4` from 30 s | graphics: flat dark background, text, a dial |

The reference HEVC rate is Frame Job's own default for the `hevc` row
(`ExporterWriter+Settings.swift` `defaultVideoBitrate`: 0.07 bits/pixel/frame):
1920×1080×30×0.07 = **4,354 kbps** (3,628 kbps for the 25p clip), keyframe at most every
2 s. HEVC was encoded by VideoToolbox through ffmpeg
(`-c:v hevc_videotoolbox -b:v 4354k -g 60 -profile:v main|main10`), the same encoder and
AverageBitRate key the `hevc`/`hevc_10bit` rows use through `AVAssetWriter`, not the same
call.

Encoder command lines (exact strings are in every `results.jsonl` row's `cmd`):

```
aomenc --good|--rt --cpu-used=N --passes=1 --end-usage=vbr --target-bitrate=K --kf-max-dist=60
       --threads=12 --row-mt=1 --tile-columns=1 [--tile-rows=1 for "Nt"] --lag-in-frames=35 (good) | 0 (rt)
       [--bit-depth=10 --input-bit-depth=10] --ivf -o out.ivf in.y4m
SvtAv1EncApp -i in.y4m -b out.ivf --preset N --rc 1 --tbr K --keyint 60 --passes 1 --progress 0
vpxenc --codec=vp9 --good|--rt --cpu-used=N --passes=1 --end-usage=vbr --target-bitrate=K --kf-max-dist=60
       --threads=12 --row-mt=1 --tile-columns=2 --frame-parallel=0

#### Recommendation (question 2)

**AV1: SVT-AV1.** Plainly, the numbers argue against libaom as the export encoder despite
the natural pull toward AOM's reference (and the owner's brother's team): at every speed an
export sheet would offer, SVT-AV1 gives more quality for the time.
- Matched quality: SVT 4 ≈ libaom good-5/6 (Δ VMAF +3.36 vs +3.67/+3.57 on `real8`, +5.11 vs
  +4.96/+4.88 on `gh5`, +3.15 vs +3.33/+3.22 at 10-bit) at ~41 fps against 13.6–16 fps:
  about 3× faster.
- Matched speed: at ~100–150 fps SVT 8 gives +2.56 against libaom rt-8's +1.37.
- libaom's best (good-3/4, +4.1–4.2 on `real8`) is ~0.8 VMAF above SVT 4 at 2.6–3.7 fps,
  about 11× slower — a 2-minute clip would take ~16 minutes.
- In libaom's favour: a higher worst-frame VMAF (92 vs 88), lower memory (0.5–1.1 GB vs
  1.0–2.1 GB), and it is AOM's reference. SVT-AV1 is also AOMedia's
  (gitlab.com/AOMediaCodec) under the same AOM patent licence.

Presets the sheet should offer for AV1 (SVT-AV1, all 1080p30 on this Mac):

| Row | SVT preset | fps 8-bit / 10-bit | Bitrate for HEVC's quality (real8 / gh5 / real10) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Faster | 8 | ~148 / ~115 | −41 % / −33 % / −32 % |
| Balanced (default) | 6 | ~75 / ~64 | −52 % / −47 % / −44 % |
| Smaller file | 4 | ~41 / ~34 | −58 % / −52 % / −56 % |

Presets 10 and 12 are within 0–0.7 VMAF of HEVC at 2–3× its CPU cost — not worth a row.

**VP9: libvpx** (the only real option), one row at `--good --cpu-used=4 --row-mt=1`

#### Recommendation (question 2)

**AV1: SVT-AV1.** Plainly, the numbers argue against libaom as the export encoder despite
the natural pull toward AOM's reference (and the owner's brother's team): at every speed an
export sheet would offer, SVT-AV1 gives more quality for the time.
- Matched quality: SVT 4 ≈ libaom good-5/6 (Δ VMAF +3.36 vs +3.67/+3.57 on `real8`, +5.11 vs
  +4.96/+4.88 on `gh5`, +3.15 vs +3.33/+3.22 at 10-bit) at ~41 fps against 13.6–16 fps:
  about 3× faster.
- Matched speed: at ~100–150 fps SVT 8 gives +2.56 against libaom rt-8's +1.37.
- libaom's best (good-3/4, +4.1–4.2 on `real8`) is ~0.8 VMAF above SVT 4 at 2.6–3.7 fps,
  about 11× slower — a 2-minute clip would take ~16 minutes.
- In libaom's favour: a higher worst-frame VMAF (92 vs 88), lower memory (0.5–1.1 GB vs
  1.0–2.1 GB), and it is AOM's reference. SVT-AV1 is also AOMedia's
  (gitlab.com/AOMediaCodec) under the same AOM patent licence.

Presets the sheet should offer for AV1 (SVT-AV1, all 1080p30 on this Mac):

| Row | SVT preset | fps 8-bit / 10-bit | Bitrate for HEVC's quality (real8 / gh5 / real10) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Faster | 8 | ~148 / ~115 | −41 % / −33 % / −32 % |
| Balanced (default) | 6 | ~75 / ~64 | −52 % / −47 % / −44 % |
| Smaller file | 4 | ~41 / ~34 | −58 % / −52 % / −56 % |

Presets 10 and 12 are within 0–0.7 VMAF of HEVC at 2–3× its CPU cost — not worth a row.

**VP9: libvpx** (the only real option), one row at `--good --cpu-used=4 --row-mt=1`

efficiency: at matched quality it needs ~1.4–1.7× SVT 6's bitrate (good-4: 3,605 vs 2,144; 2,774 vs 1,989; 3,714 vs 2,452 kbps).

### 7. HDR

| | HEVC rows today | AV1 | VP9 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Profile | Main 10 | Main (profile 0), 10-bit | Profile 2 |
| Colour in the bitstream | VUI | sequence header `color_config`: `AV1E_SET_COLOR_PRIMARIES/TRANSFER_CHARACTERISTICS/MATRIX_COEFFICIENTS` (libaom), `color_primaries`/`transfer_characteristics` in SVT's config — measured: aomenc `--transfer-characteristics=hlg` gave an MP4 ffprobe reads as `arib-std-b67` with no container tags | only `color_space` (BT.709/BT.2020…, `VP9E_SET_COLOR_SPACE`), **no transfer** — HLG/PQ must come from the container |
| MP4 tags | `colr` from `AVVideoColorPropertiesKey` | `colr` from the description's extensions — measured HLG and PQ | `vpcC` carries primaries/transfer/matrix — measured HLG |
| HDR10 metadata (HD-5's fixed values) | VT compression keys | `mdcv`/`clli` boxes from `MasteringDisplayColorVolume`/`ContentLightLevelInfo` extensions — measured written and read back; in-band metadata OBUs available (`aom_img_add_metadata` with `OBU_METADATA_TYPE_HDR_MDCV/CLL`, SVT `mastering_display`/`content_light_level`), not exercised; AV1-ISOBMFF says the boxes SHOULD be present and SHALL equal the OBUs | MP4 boxes as for AV1; WebM `Colour/MasteringMetadata` + `MaxCLL`/`MaxFALL` — measured with libwebm and read back by the core |
| WebM tags | — | `Colour` element — measured HLG | `Colour` element — measured PQ |

So the new 10-bit rows can take `hevc_10bit`'s place in H-3's rules (`"hdr": true`,
`dynamic_range` hlg/pq/sdr), with the tags written in both the bitstream (AV1) and the
container. No Dolby Vision question arises. Not measured: any player's HDR rendering of
these files.

### Risks

1. **Speed.** Software AV1 is 1.5–5.4× (SVT 8–4) slower than VideoToolbox HEVC per 1080p frame
   here (148–41 fps against ~222) and needs 1.0–2.1 GB; 4K is untested and will be ~4× the work. The sheet must say
   so (an estimate), and the Export Queue must not run two SVT jobs at once on a 16 GB Mac
   without measuring it.
2. **No AV1 decode on M1/M2**: Frame Job cannot preview or re-import its own AV1 export
   there (#216 refuses it), QuickTime won't play it, and proofs must check AV1 output with
   ffmpeg/dav1d. Only an M3+ can confirm playback (a manual-checks row).
3. **`av01` brand missing** from AVAssetWriter's `ftyp`; the in-place patch is a small byte
   rewrite after `finishWriting` that has to be right on every file (moov-first too).
4. **Rate accuracy**: 1-pass VBR undershot by up to 22 % on 5 s clips; an explicit
   `video_bitrate` will not be met exactly, and the "encoder decides" default needs an AV1
   rule (HEVC's 0.07 bpp is ~2× what SVT 6 needs for the same VMAF here).
5. **WebM is a second writer**, against §7.8's one-writer argument: chapters, range, size,
   the #337 audio length rule and graphic failures must hold there too.
6. **Alpha**: only Chrome/Firefox (Safari unconfirmed), ffmpeg's default VP9 decoder drops
   it, and Frame Job's own import drops VP9 alpha (#216-R) — an alpha WebM cannot come back
   in with its alpha.
7. **Build**: cmake on every build machine and the publish runner (runner not measured);
   perl from the OS; ~2 min clean build; network or a tarball cache for the sources.
8. **Licence duties**: BSD notices and the AOM patent licence text in the acknowledgements
   (#376); the AOM and Google grants terminate for a party that sues.
9. **VMAF caveats**: VMAF is not calibrated for HLG code values (`real8`/`real10`) and
   saturates on graphics (`promo`); clips are 5 s; HEVC was driven through ffmpeg rather than
   AVAssetWriter.
10. **WebM timing**: libwebm's default millisecond times and the reader's grid rule
    disagreed (grid false even with DefaultDuration, as for ffmpeg's WebM).

### Risks

1. **Speed.** Software AV1 is 1.5–5.4× (SVT 8–4) slower than VideoToolbox HEVC per 1080p frame
   here (148–41 fps against ~222) and needs 1.0–2.1 GB; 4K is untested and will be ~4× the work. The sheet must say
   so (an estimate), and the Export Queue must not run two SVT jobs at once on a 16 GB Mac
   without measuring it.
2. **No AV1 decode on M1/M2**: Frame Job cannot preview or re-import its own AV1 export
   there (#216 refuses it), QuickTime won't play it, and proofs must check AV1 output with
   ffmpeg/dav1d. Only an M3+ can confirm playback (a manual-checks row).
3. **`av01` brand missing** from AVAssetWriter's `ftyp`; the in-place patch is a small byte
   rewrite after `finishWriting` that has to be right on every file (moov-first too).
4. **Rate accuracy**: 1-pass VBR undershot by up to 22 % on 5 s clips; an explicit
   `video_bitrate` will not be met exactly, and the "encoder decides" default needs an AV1
   rule (HEVC's 0.07 bpp is ~2× what SVT 6 needs for the same VMAF here).
5. **WebM is a second writer**, against §7.8's one-writer argument: chapters, range, size,
   the #337 audio length rule and graphic failures must hold there too.
6. **Alpha**: only Chrome/Firefox (Safari unconfirmed), ffmpeg's default VP9 decoder drops
   it, and Frame Job's own import drops VP9 alpha (#216-R) — an alpha WebM cannot come back
   in with its alpha.
7. **Build**: cmake on every build machine and the publish runner (runner not measured);
   perl from the OS; ~2 min clean build; network or a tarball cache for the sources.
8. **Licence duties**: BSD notices and the AOM patent licence text in the acknowledgements
   (#376); the AOM and Google grants terminate for a party that sues.
9. **VMAF caveats**: VMAF is not calibrated for HLG code values (`real8`/`real10`) and
   saturates on graphics (`promo`); clips are 5 s; HEVC was driven through ffmpeg rather than
   AVAssetWriter.
10. **WebM timing**: libwebm's default millisecond times and the reader's grid rule
    disagreed (grid false even with DefaultDuration, as for ffmpeg's WebM).

every measured file at or under it (12 % overshoot), the owner's clip at Faster did not reach
HEVC's VMAF at any CRF. The owner then chose **"Quality first, soft cap"** (2026-10-28): SVT's
default 50 % overshoot, the rate a soft cap with its measured maximum, R1 and R2 holding each
file to at most 1.25 × the cap and at or above `hevc`'s VMAF. That is built, and the Release
`--rate` run passes 15/15 (below, "Ruling 2"). Everything else in the pass is done.

**The owner's decision, built.** CX-13 records capped constant quality before the code:
SVT-AV1 at `rate_control_mode` 0, `aq_mode` 2, `qp` the CRF and `max_bit_rate` the cap
(`video_bitrate`, else HEVC's 0.07 bits per pixel per frame, at most 100,000 kb/s), as
SVT-AV1 v4.2.0's `EbSvtAv1Enc.h` ("Capped CRF") and `enc_settings.c` (the max bit rate
refused outside mode 0) and `enc_handle.c` (single-pass VBR forces KF refresh, `lap_rc`)
show. The CRF is `SVTAV1Encoder.crf(speed:bitsPerPixel:)`: CX-13's table, linear in the
cap's bits per pixel per frame, rounded down. `mbr_over_shoot_pct` was 12 until Ruling 2
put it back to SVT's 50. The guide's Quality list, limits and agent table, the MCP page, the
sheet's tier titles and footnote (`ExportSheetResolve.swift`) and `video_bitrate`'s catalog
description first said the rate was a ceiling ("up to …"); after Ruling 2 they say it is a
soft cap the file usually stays under ("usually ≤ …"), with one sentence naming the
measured overshoot (about 1.25 ×). `av1_export_proof.py`'s R1 and R2 now export the owner's clip as
`prores_422` (the reference), `hevc` and `av1` at each speed, at "Format default" and High,
and ask each `av1` file to average at most 1.25 × the cap (Ruling 2; first at or under it)
and to score a VMAF at or above `hevc`'s.

**The calibration** (`tools/proof/work/codec-spike/crf.py`, `crf_owner.py`, all rows in
`crf.jsonl`; a shared machine, load averages 30–38 during the owner runs):

  8, 6 and 4, CRF 18–46 in steps of 2, uncapped: 135 encodes. The highest CRF reaching
  HEVC's VMAF on all three clips was, Low to Maximum, Faster 40/28/26/26/18, Balanced
  44/34/32/30/24, Smaller file 46/38/34/30/24.

  overshoot (Medium and up); at 10 % gh5 at Faster's Medium fell 0.020 under HEVC; 25 % reached

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Codec export C1 fix pass (spec §11 CX-13): calibrate the `av1` row's CRF on the
owner's IMG_0018.MOV through Frame Job itself, since the spike's command-line
encodes of a decoded file do not transfer to the app's own frames.

crf_owner.py [--reuse]

Builds a Release copy of the tree (`tree_copy`, in `work/crf-owner-tree/`) whose
`SVTAV1Encoder` takes its CRF from the file `work/crf-owner/crf` when that holds a
number (an instrument only, never in the tree), launches it, makes the owner
clip's 1920 × 1080 30 fps project, exports `prores_422` (the reference, as
`av1_export_proof.py` R does), `hevc` at the five calibration rates, and `av1` at
each speed and CRF 12..30 step 2 with a cap of 50 Mb/s (so the cap never binds),
and scores each against the reference with ffmpeg's libvmaf. Appends to
`crf.jsonl` (`clip` "owner", `via` "app").
"""
import json, os, subprocess, sys, time
from pathlib import Path

S = Path("/Users/kevingalligan/devel/framejob-codecs/tools/proof/work/codec-spike")
PROOF = S.parents[1]
sys.path.insert(0, str(PROOF))
sys.path.insert(0, str(PROOF / "graphics_spike"))
import bounded  # noqa: E402
import mcp  # noqa: E402
import proof_app  # noqa: E402
import tree_copy  # noqa: E402

WORK = PROOF / "work" / "crf-owner"
TREE = PROOF / "work" / "crf-owner-tree"
CRF_FILE = WORK / "crf"
OWNER = PROOF / "media" / "owner-sync" / "IMG_0018.MOV"
LOG = S / "crf.jsonl"
RATES = {"low": 2_400_000, "medium": 3_600_000, "default": 4_354_560, "high": 4_800_000,
         "maximum": 7_200_000}
RELEASE = "a Debug build composes the 55 s clip too slowly to calibrate on"
ANCHOR = "        config.qp = Self.crf(speed: speed, bitsPerPixel: Double(cap)\n"
PATCH = ("        config.qp = (try? String(contentsOfFile: \"" + str(CRF_FILE) + "\", encoding: .utf8))"
         ".flatMap { UInt32($0.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)) }"
         " ?? Self.crf(speed: speed, bitsPerPixel: Double(cap)\n")


def build():
    made, reason = tree_copy.make_copy(str(TREE))
    if made is None:
        raise SystemExit(f"copy: {reason}")
    path = TREE / "app/Sources/ExportAV1Encoder.swift"
    text = path.read_text()
    assert text.count(ANCHOR) == 1, "anchor"
    path.write_text(text.replace(ANCHOR, PATCH))
    app, reason = tree_copy.build_app(TREE, 1800, release_only=RELEASE)
    if app is None:
        raise SystemExit(f"build: {reason}")
    return app


def vmaf(distorted, reference, tag):
    log = WORK / f"{tag}.vmaf.json"
    lavfi = ("[0:v]format=yuv420p,setpts=PTS-STARTPTS[d];[1:v]format=yuv420p,setpts=PTS-STARTPTS[r];"
             f"[d][r]libvmaf=log_fmt=json:log_path={log}:n_threads=12")

def run_dt(client, state):
    """DT: every video row of an HLG project at its default and each accepted
    dynamic_range, tagged as the picture it writes; no Dolby Vision in any HEVC file."""
    misses, figures = [], []
    doc = hlg_doc(client, "dt", [fixture("hlg")])
    for preset in VIDEO_ROWS:
        ranges = [None, "hlg", "pq", "sdr"] if preset in HDR_ROWS else [None, "sdr"]
        for asked in ranges:
            tag = f"dt-{preset}-{asked or 'default'}"
            extra = {"dynamic_range": asked} if asked else {}
            path, got = export_as(doc, tag, preset, **extra)
            picture = asked or ("hlg" if preset in HDR_ROWS else "sdr")
            said = reply(got).get("dynamic_range")
            if path is None:
                misses.append(f"{tag}: {got.get('error', 'no file')}")
                continue
            if said != picture:
                misses.append(f"{tag}: the result's dynamic_range {said!r}, not {picture!r}")
            if preset in ("gif", "apng"):
                figures.append(f"{tag}: written ({path.stat().st_size} bytes)")
                continue
            read = tags(stream(path))
            line = f"{tag}: {read}"
            if read != PICTURE_TAGS[picture]:
                misses.append(f"{tag}: {read}, not {PICTURE_TAGS[picture]}")
            if preset.startswith("hevc"):
                record, rpu = dovi(path)
                line += f", DOVI record {record}, RPU {rpu}"
                if record or rpu:
                    misses.append(f"{tag}: Dolby Vision")
            figures.append(line)
    state["dt_closed"] = doc.close()
    check("DT every video row of an HLG project (the hlg ramp, 1 s) at its default and each "
          "accepted dynamic_range: bt709 ×3 for the SDR version, bt2020nc/arib-std-b67/bt2020 "
          "for hlg, bt2020nc/smpte2084/bt2020 for pq, the result naming it; no DOVI record or "
          "RPU in any HEVC file; gif and apng written", not misses,
          f"failed {misses or 'none'}\n       " + "\n       ".join(figures))


def run_dp(client, state):
    """DP: the three 10-bit rows at pq carry HD-5's mastering display and content light
    level; prores_422's decoded grey row = the PQ oracle ±2/1023."""
    misses, figures = [], []
    path = fixture("hlg")
    source = yuv_frames(path, W, H) if path else None
    doc = hlg_doc(client, "dp", [path])
    outs = {preset: export_as(doc, f"dp-{preset}", preset, dynamic_range="pq")
            for preset in HDR_ROWS}
    state["dp_closed"] = doc.close()
    for preset, (out, got) in outs.items():
        if out is None:
            misses.append(f"{preset}: {got.get('error', 'no file')}")
            continue
        found = side_all(out)
        figures.append(f"{preset}: {tags(stream(out))}; side data {found}")
        wrong = {k: found.get(k) for k, v in HDR10_SIDE.items() if found.get(k) != v}
        if wrong:
            misses.append(f"{preset}: {wrong}")
    out = outs["prores_422"][0]
    frames = yuv_frames(out, W, H, 16) if out else None
          "prores_422 {sdr} frame 15 ±1/255 on the grey row every 8th column; a JPEG "
          "render_frame (no sdr_version) = the sdr_version PNG ±1/255, labelled as it",

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Road map "codec-export" C1 — the `av1` row: AV1 in MP4 through the bundled
SVT-AV1 (spec §11 CX-1, CX-2, CX-9, CX-10, CX-12, CX-13).

    python3 tools/proof/av1_export_proof.py [--app debug|release|PATH] [--rate]
    python3 tools/proof/av1_export_proof.py --mutant NAME

Launches its own instances of the chosen app (`proof_app.py`: `--app`, else
`RC_PROOF_APP`, else Debug; a build older than its inputs is refused) on scratch
sockets, works under `tools/proof/work/av1-export/`, closes every project it opens

Phase 2 adds sound. The three movies above are silent, and a clip of a
silent movie has NO audio group (an `.m4a` clip has no video group), so the
solo proof needs two tones it can tell apart by ear and by byte, and the
paste-attributes proof needs one clip that has BOTH groups:

```sh
ffmpeg -y -f lavfi -i "sine=frequency=440:sample_rate=48000:duration=5" -ac 2 -c:a aac -b:a 128k toneA.m4a
ffmpeg -y -f lavfi -i "sine=frequency=880:sample_rate=48000:duration=5" -ac 2 -c:a aac -b:a 128k toneB.m4a
ffmpeg -y -f lavfi -i "testsrc=size=640x360:rate=30:duration=5" \
       -f lavfi -i "sine=frequency=440:sample_rate=48000:duration=5" \
       -ac 2 -pix_fmt yuv420p -c:v libx264 -c:a aac -b:a 128k -shortest AV.mov
```

(5 s, 48 kHz stereo AAC; `AV.mov` is the test card with the 440 Hz tone
under it.) `phase2_proof.py` also runs `ffmpeg` at proof time, to decode
each `audio_m4a` export to raw PCM


# ---- the instance ----------------------------------------------------------------

class Instance:
    def __init__(self, label, app, arguments=(), env=None, home=False):
        self.label = label
        self.dir = WORK / label
        tree_copy.remove_tree(str(self.dir))
        self.dir.mkdir(parents=True)
        self.log = self.dir / "instance.log"
        if home:
            (self.dir / "home").mkdir()
            env = {**(env or {}), "CFFIXED_USER_HOME": str(self.dir / "home")}
        self.launched = mcp.launch(str(proof_app.executable(app)), list(arguments),
                                   env=bounded.child_env(env or {}), log_path=str(self.log),
                                   timeout=900)
        self.client = self.launched.client

    def stop(self):
        self.launched.stop()
        mcp.remove_scratch(self.launched.socket_path)

    def complaints(self):
        try:
            lines = self.log.read_text(errors="replace").splitlines()
        except OSError:
            return ["the log could not be read"]
        return [line.strip() for line in lines
                if "Frame Job: " in line or "Svt[" in line or "SVT-AV1: " in line]


class Doc:
    def __init__(self, instance, name, width=640, height=360):
        self.client = instance.client
        self.path = str(instance.dir / f"{name}.framejob")
        self.client.call("new_project", path=self.path)
        try:
            self.call("set_canvas", width=width, height=height, fps=30)
        except mcp.ToolError as error:
            if "made no change" not in str(error):    # a new project is 1920 × 1080 at 30
                raise

    def call(self, tool, **arguments):
        return self.client.call_with(tool, {"project": self.path, **arguments})

    def track(self):
        return self.call("get_project")["project"]["tracks"][0]["id"]

    def media(self, path):
        return self.call("import_media", path=str(path))["media"]

    def close(self):
        try:
            self.call("close_project", discard=True)
        except mcp.ToolError:
            pass


def av_doc(instance, name):
    """AV.mov from 0 under a two-second text clip on a track of its own."""
    doc = Doc(instance, name)
    media = doc.media(AV)
    doc.call("add_clip", track=doc.track(), media=media, at=0)
    doc.call("add_track", name="Titles")
    titles = doc.call("get_project")["project"]["tracks"][-1]["id"]
    doc.call("add_text_clip", track=titles, at=0, duration=2 * SEC, text={"content": "AV1"})
    return doc


def export(doc, path, **arguments):
    Path(path).unlink(missing_ok=True)
    return doc.client.export_with({"project": doc.path, "path": str(path), **arguments})


def refusal(doc, path, **arguments):
    Path(path).unlink(missing_ok=True)
    try:
        answer = doc.client.call_with("export", {"project": doc.path, "path": str(path),
                                                 **arguments})
    except mcp.ToolError as error:
        return str(error)
    if isinstance(answer, dict) and "export_id" in answer:
        try:
            doc.client.wait_export(answer["export_id"], seconds=300)
        except mcp.ToolError:
            pass
    return None


# ---- the rows --------------------------------------------------------------------

def rows_a1_a5(doc, out):
    a1 = out / "a1.mp4"
    try:
        done = export(doc, a1, preset="av1")
    except mcp.ToolError as error:
        for ident in ("A1", "A2", "A3a", "A3b", "A4", "A5"):
            check(ident, False, f"A1's export failed: {error}")
        return
    got = streams(a1)
    video = next((s for s in got if s.get("codec_type") == "video"), {})
    audio = next((s for s in got if s.get("codec_type") == "audio"), {})
    seen = (video.get("codec_name"), video.get("codec_tag_string"), video.get("profile"),
            video.get("pix_fmt"), video.get("width"), video.get("height"),
            audio.get("codec_name"), audio.get("codec_tag_string"))
    want = ("av1", "av01", "Main", "yuv420p", 640, 360, "aac", "mp4a")
    length = float(video.get("duration") or 0)
    check("A1", done.get("status") == "done" and seen == want and abs(length - 5) <= 1 / 30,
          f"status {done.get('status')}, {done.get('bytes')} bytes; read {seen} (want {want}); "
          f"video {length:.3f} s")
    found = brands(a1)
    check("A2", "av01" in found, f"compatible brands {found!r}")

    head, per_packet = trace(a1)
    every = head + [f for p in per_packet for f in p["fields"]]
    names = ("color_description_present_flag", "color_primaries", "transfer_characteristics",
             "matrix_coefficients", "color_range")
    values = {n: sorted({v for k, v in every if k == n}) for n in names}
    check("A3a", values == {names[0]: [1], names[1]: [1], names[2]: [1], names[3]: [1],
                            names[4]: [0]},
          f"the sequence headers' {values}")
    colr = colr_of(a1)

# ---- the instance ----------------------------------------------------------------

class Instance:
    def __init__(self, label, app, arguments=(), env=None, home=False):
        self.label = label
        self.dir = WORK / label
        tree_copy.remove_tree(str(self.dir))
        self.dir.mkdir(parents=True)
        self.log = self.dir / "instance.log"
        if home:
            (self.dir / "home").mkdir()
            env = {**(env or {}), "CFFIXED_USER_HOME": str(self.dir / "home")}
        self.launched = mcp.launch(str(proof_app.executable(app)), list(arguments),
                                   env=bounded.child_env(env or {}), log_path=str(self.log),
                                   timeout=900)
        self.client = self.launched.client

    def stop(self):
        self.launched.stop()
        mcp.remove_scratch(self.launched.socket_path)

    def complaints(self):
        try:
            lines = self.log.read_text(errors="replace").splitlines()
        except OSError:
            return ["the log could not be read"]
        return [line.strip() for line in lines
                if "Frame Job: " in line or "Svt[" in line or "SVT-AV1: " in line]


class Doc:
    def __init__(self, instance, name, width=640, height=360):
        self.client = instance.client
        self.path = str(instance.dir / f"{name}.framejob")
        self.client.call("new_project", path=self.path)
        try:
            self.call("set_canvas", width=width, height=height, fps=30)
        except mcp.ToolError as error:
            if "made no change" not in str(error):    # a new project is 1920 × 1080 at 30
                raise

    def call(self, tool, **arguments):
        return self.client.call_with(tool, {"project": self.path, **arguments})

    def track(self):
        return self.call("get_project")["project"]["tracks"][0]["id"]

    def media(self, path):
        return self.call("import_media", path=str(path))["media"]

    def close(self):
        try:
            self.call("close_project", discard=True)
        except mcp.ToolError:
            pass


def av_doc(instance, name):
    """AV.mov from 0 under a two-second text clip on a track of its own."""
    doc = Doc(instance, name)
    media = doc.media(AV)
    doc.call("add_clip", track=doc.track(), media=media, at=0)
    doc.call("add_track", name="Titles")
    titles = doc.call("get_project")["project"]["tracks"][-1]["id"]
    doc.call("add_text_clip", track=titles, at=0, duration=2 * SEC, text={"content": "AV1"})
    return doc


def export(doc, path, **arguments):
    Path(path).unlink(missing_ok=True)
    return doc.client.export_with({"project": doc.path, "path": str(path), **arguments})


def refusal(doc, path, **arguments):
    Path(path).unlink(missing_ok=True)
    try:
        answer = doc.client.call_with("export", {"project": doc.path, "path": str(path),
                                                 **arguments})
    except mcp.ToolError as error:
        return str(error)
    if isinstance(answer, dict) and "export_id" in answer:
        try:
            doc.client.wait_export(answer["export_id"], seconds=300)
        except mcp.ToolError:

    return None
